The two open findings on242

242-A,01M8CBTK24SEXGTB8EGW6HAHVX,low: advisory output can replace the command result.

PendingWork is documented as non-failing, but write_notes/write_unchecked_note returnResult and release call sites propagate?. A successful dry-run report can be written before the advisory turns the run into failure. On an E169 path, that I/O failure replaces the primary domain error before main receives it.

We ran12 exact-head Text/JSON cases with normal-output controls and closedstderr. Pending-found,unchecked-pending,nothing-to-release and actual-no-effect controls exit0; closedstderr makesJSON exit1 andText panic101. E169 controls normally return1; source tracing proves the replacement, while a closed error sink naturally cannot display which error was substituted. An injected writer regression must assert the returned typed error directly.

The whole-class sweep found the same problem in raw release warning macros, init's unchecked advisory, Text error-card rendering and runner echo. A missing-remote-tag advisory panics before either Text orJSON preview. help nonexistent normally exits2; closedstderr Text exits101 whileJSON preserves2. Runner capture_stream echoes before completing its capture/send; an echo panic can kill the reader, lose classifier output and fabricate an incomplete-pipe command failure. That runner sibling is source-traced, not a claim that a real publication was executed.

Correction: one narrowly named best-effort stderr presentation operation, used for advisory/diagnostic echo and final error rendering. It must not replace the already selected result or stop a child-output reader from draining and capturing. Make the advisory API non-failing and migrate every consumer, including init and origin-tag advice. Preserve Notes collection, report membership and exactly-once normal emission. Required prompt/review failures, storage writes, receipt/intent commits, actual process errors and real capture failures remain authoritative. Do not blanket-ignore all I/O or all init output.

242-B,01M8CBTK1EY23ERNRKHJVDYV5B,low: the process-count test does not isolate advisory work.

The fixture puts each package's current-version tag atHEAD. releases_tagged_at resolves those tags before comparing them withHEAD. Older Git bulk-tag output leaves a nested tag unresolved, so that legitimate resumption check costs a process per package independently of inference.

Claude's proposed correction,putting the SAME current-version tag on an older commit,was tested and remains insufficient:

Keep native and legacy-output controls. Do not infer advisory cost from an unqualified whole-command total.

The two open findings on246

246-A,01M8CB6ME1QENKZGQC3M4GWZ4M,low: duplicate validation is quadratic.

For each unique entry,the writer scans all earlier entries. N entries requireN(N-1)/2 name comparisons before considering name length.10,000 entries mean49,995,000 comparisons per serialization. The wizard serializes twice,but repeated pure serialization is not itself a correctness defect.

The same algorithm exists in flag ingestion:each resolved --package scans earlier entries. Fix both. The parser already has a seen-name map and is a useful existing pattern. Retain output order,the first offending index,error precedence,existing E268/E329 behavior,reader-based representability and summary canonicalization.

Correction: one-pass standard HashSet membership in the writer,borrowing names from its immutable slice; a separate set keyed by resolved owner identity in flag ingestion so aliases of the same owner still conflict. These are distinct semantic checks,not a reason for a generic duplicate framework. Preserve iteration order by using the set only for membership.

Tests:valid bytes unchanged;duplicate at beginning/middle/end;earlier unrepresentable name still wins;two selectors for one owner;large unique input;existing properties. MeasureN/2N/4N for engineering evidence; avoid flaky wall-time CI thresholds. The current exact algorithm proves the defect; no isolated writer timing benchmark was falsely claimed.

246-B,01M8CB6MDFSS95H6CMX6857A25,low: tokenization can change the chosen package.

The shared picker splits whitespace/commas before identity resolution. In exact-head PTY probes,typing trail-space or qualified npm/trail-space selected,wrote and subsequently attributed pending work to the SHORTtrail package. Row2 in the same roster correctly preserved trail-space. Internal-space and comma names expose the same representational boundary. Quoted input is currently rejected. The problem is not just an inconvenient spelling:the selected identity changes.

The review screen is a chance for a person to catch that error;it does not make the selector correct. Documentation alone cannot close it. The no-new-grammar instruction also does not authorize identity substitution.

Required invariant:accepted selection preserves the intended resolved identity;unsupported or ambiguous text is rejected before producing a selection. Two bounded policies can satisfy it:

A.Keep no new token grammar. Prompts containing separator-bearing names must have an enforceable policy such as an explicitly announced rows-only mode that bypasses textualNameLookup. Reject textual answers rather than splitting them into other packages. Normal rosters keep current semantics. Explicitly document/test the numeric-name behavior of this mode;do not silently change exact-name priority.

B.Intentionally support lossless quoted identity tokens. Use JSON double-quoted strings decoded by existingserde_json,not a second escape implementation or shell expansion. Preserve decoded whitespace and quotedness;quoted"1" is an identity and never falls back to row1. Keep current unquoted number/range/name semantics,commas/whitespace outside quotes,and exact-name precedence. Reject malformed strings and a missing separator after a closingquote. Print copyable selectors and document the syntax. Implement once before the sharedNameLookup so add and init both benefit;preserve the existing product alias/ambiguity authority.

Recommendation:B gives the more consistent long-term CLI. A is a valid smaller fix if the owner retains no-new-grammar.
